newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy PM says rate cut will help economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Italy PM says rate cut will help economic growth.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi welcomed the Bank of Italy's official discount rate cut, saying it would spur the economy.
"The decision by the Bank of Italy will give a new impulse to development and the economic pick-up as well as employment in the country," a statement from the prime minister's office said.
The central bank cut its discount rate to 6.75 percent from 7.5 percent, while the fixed term advances rate was lowered to 8.25 percent from nine percent.
"Italy has not seen such a low discount rate for over 20 years," deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni said in a statement. "It is an extraordinary result which rewards the government's policies."
The Bank of Italy has cut the discount rate three times over the last six months.
